Metacommunity data in one object

Source: R/mc_data.R
mc_data.Rd

Keeps the community and what describes its species and sites together, with names checked once. The analyses accept an mc_data object as their first argument and take from it what the call leaves out, so pcps_test(d) uses d$tree and d$env. Simulations convert with as_mc_data().

Usage

mc_data(
  comm,
  tree = NULL,
  traits = NULL,
  env = NULL,
  coords = NULL,
  areas = NULL,
  series = NULL
)

as_mc_data(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_mc_data(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mc_data'
as_mc_data(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mc_sim'
as_mc_data(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mc_data'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mc_data'
x[i, j, drop = FALSE]

# S3 method for class 'mc_data'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mc_data'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

comm

Matrix or data frame with one row per site and one column per species, named by species. Sites without names are called site1, site2 and so on.

tree

Optional phylo object.

traits

Optional data frame, matrix or named vector with one row per species, named by species.

env

Optional data frame, matrix or vector with one row per site.

coords

Optional matrix or data frame of coordinates with one row per site.

areas

Optional vector with the area or biogeographic event of each site, for biogeography_matrix().

series

Optional array of sites x species x steps, such as the history of a simulation.

x, object

An mc_data object, or for as_mc_data() an object to convert.

...

Passed to mc_data() by as_mc_data(); not used elsewhere.

i, j

Sites and species to keep, by position, name or logical vector.

drop, row.names, optional

Not used.

Value

mc_data() and as_mc_data() give a list of class mc_data with comm, tree, traits (data frame), env (data frame), coords (matrix), areas and series, each NULL when absent. [ gives the same for a subset, summary() gives summary_stats() and as.data.frame() a long table with site, species, step (NA without series) and abundance, without absences.

Details

Species are matched by name between comm, tree and traits, and those missing from any of them are dropped with a warning, as in the analyses. Species without individuals stay, since they belong to the regional pool. Sites are matched by name when env, coords, areas or series have names, and by position otherwise.

Examples

set.seed(1)
tree <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(12)
traits <- species_traits(tree, lambda = 1, optima_range = c(0, 100), rmax_range = c(0, 30))
env <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 20)
comm <- simulate_static(traits, env, incidence = TRUE)$abundance
d <- mc_data(comm, tree, traits["optimum"], env = data.frame(env = env))
d
#> <mc_data> 20 sites x 12 species
#> tree: 12 tips
#> traits: optimum
#> env: env
d[1:10, ]
#> <mc_data> 10 sites x 12 species
#> tree: 12 tips
#> traits: optimum
#> env: env
pcps_test(d[rowSums(d$comm) > 0, ], n_perm = 9)
#> <mc_pcps> principal coordinates of phylogenetic structure
#> permutations: 9 free of sites, 9 of species; smallest possible p: 0.1
#>   test share    r2 statistic p_site p_species p_max
#>  whole 1.000 0.235      5.53    0.1       0.5   0.5
#>  pcps1 0.277 0.735     49.95    0.1       0.2   0.2
#>  pcps2 0.237 0.093      1.84    0.1       0.6   0.6
